test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 16 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A diver rowing at the speed of 3 km/h in still water takes double the time going 50 km upstream compared to going 50 km downstream. The speed of the stream is:
solution:
**Given:**

Speed in still water = 3 km/h

Time is taken double in going 50 km upstream compared to going 50 km downstream

**Concept Used:**

Upstream speed = Speed in still water – Speed of stream

Downstream speed = Speed in still water + Speed of stream

Time = (Distance)/(Speed)

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of the stream be x.

Upstream speed = 3 – x

Downstream speed = 3 + x

Time is taken going upstream = (50)/(3-x)

Time is taken going downstream = (50)/(3+x)

According to the question,

⇒ (50)/(3-x)=2×(50)/(3+x)

⇒ (50)/(3-x)=(100)/(3+x)

⇒ (1)/(3-x)=(2)/(3+x)

⇒ 3 + x = 2 × (3 - x)

⇒ x + 2x = 6 - 3

⇒ 3x = 3

⇒ x = 1 km/h

**Therefore, the speed of the stream is 1 km/h.**

Hence, the correct answer is **option 2).**
